label: SMA 50
description: Simple average of the last 50 closes.
reading: The average of the last 50 closes, redrawn each bar. Price above a rising 50 is read as a healthy medium-term uptrend; a cross below is an early warning. It lags by design: it smooths out noise by reacting late.

label: SMA 200
description: Simple average of the last 200 closes: the long-term trend.
reading: The average of the last 200 closes: the most widely watched long-term trend line. Above it is called a bull market, below it a bear market, and a cross often makes headlines. On daily bars it reacts slowly, so it misses the first part of every move. Kestrel's best result, trend-vol-target, uses a similar idea (is the close above where it was 20, 60 and 120 days ago?) and cut drawdowns, but couldn't be told apart from luck.

label: EMA 20
description: Exponential average of the last 20 closes.
reading: Like a moving average, but recent closes count for more (each bar's weight is 2/21), so it turns sooner than a simple average of the same length. Traders use it as a short-term trend line and a place pullbacks often pause. Turning sooner also means more false turns.

label: Bollinger 20, 2
description: SMA 20 with bands 2 standard deviations either side: wide when the market is wild.
reading: A 20-bar average with bands two standard deviations above and below. The bands widen when prices swing wildly and squeeze together when they're calm; a squeeze is often followed by a big move, but not in a predictable direction. A close outside a band is unusual, not a signal by itself: in a strong trend price can ride the band for weeks.

label: RSI 14
description: Relative strength index: 0-100, the share of recent movement that was up. Above 70 is called overbought, below 30 oversold.
reading: Compares the size of recent up-moves with recent down-moves over 14 bars (Wilder's smoothing) on a 0 to 100 scale: 100 means every move was up. Above 70 is called overbought, below 30 oversold. In crypto trends RSI can stay overbought for months, so 'overbought, sell' often sells early. Kestrel's buy-the-dip ideas (reversals after big down days, Fear & Greed contrarian) lost to holding.

label: MACD 12, 26, 9
description: EMA 12 minus EMA 26, with a 9-bar EMA of that as its signal line.
reading: The 12-bar EMA minus the 26-bar EMA (the MACD line), a 9-bar EMA of that line (the signal), and their difference (the histogram). MACD above zero means the short-term average is above the long-term one; crossing the signal line is read as momentum turning. It's built from moving averages, so it lags like them.

label: ATR 14
description: Average true range: how far the price typically moves in a bar.
reading: Average true range: how far price typically travels in a bar, including gaps from the previous close, smoothed over 14 bars. It doesn't say which way. It's used to size positions and set stops at a distance the market's normal noise won't hit. Kestrel's crash brake used 2 ATR; it was triggered by ordinary swings and made both strategies worse.

label: Volatility 30d
description: Annualised volatility of the last 30 days of returns.
reading: How much daily returns varied over the last 30 days, scaled to a year (annualised standard deviation). Bitcoin usually runs between 40% and 80%. Trend-vol-target holds less when this is high; the test showed its edge came from the trend votes, not from this sizing.

label: Relative volume 20
description: This bar's volume over the average of the 20 before it: 1 is normal, 3 is triple.
reading: This bar's volume divided by the average volume of the 20 bars before it. 1 is a normal bar, 3 is three times normal. Breakouts on high relative volume are read as more convincing. Volume on one exchange is only part of the market, and big moves bring volume whichever way they go.

label: On-balance volume
description: Volume added on up closes, subtracted on down closes. Only its direction matters.
reading: A running total that adds a bar's volume when it closes up and subtracts it when it closes down. The level means nothing (it depends on where the chart starts); only its direction does. A rising OBV while price is flat is read as buyers quietly accumulating.

label: Distance from SMA 200
description: How far the close is above or below its 200-bar average.
reading: How far the close is above (+) or below (-) its 200-bar average, as a percentage. Big positive readings mean an extended run (often late in a rally); big negative readings mean a deep drop below trend. Useful for comparing how stretched the market is now with past peaks and troughs.
